claim.summary: src/click/shell_completion.py implements Click's shell completion. shell_complete() parses an instruction such as "bash_source" or "zsh_complete" from an env var. It looks up a ShellComplete subclass in the `_available_shells` registry. It then either prints the shell script (`source`) or the formatted completions (`complete`). Completion resolves a Context chain from the already-typed args (`_resolve_context`), picks the object that completes the incomplete word (`_resolve_incomplete`), and calls that object's `shell_complete(ctx, incomplete)`. That call returns a list of CompletionItem. Each shell subclass supplies a script template (`source_template`), env-var parsing (`get_completion_args`) and an output wire format (`format_completion`). Wire formats: bash and fish use "type,value" lines (fish adds a tab and help), while zsh and powershell use 3-line "type\nvalue\nhelp" records with "_" as the no-help sentinel. Custom shells can be registered with add_completion_class.

interfaces.name: shell_complete
interfaces.behavior: Entry point (line 19). Splits `instruction` with partition('_') into shell and instruction. Looks up the class with get_completion_class, instantiates it as comp_cls(cli, ctx_args, prog_name, complete_var), and returns 0 or 1. 'source' echoes comp.source() as encoded bytes with nl=False. 'complete' echoes comp.complete() as encoded bytes, with a trailing newline. Bytes are written so Windows does not turn LF into CRLF.
edge_cases: Unknown shell returns 1
Unknown instruction returns 1
Instruction without '_' gives shell=whole string and instruction='' so it returns 1 (or 1 for unknown shell)
The shell name is the part before the first underscore, so registered names containing '_' can never match

interfaces.name: CompletionItem
interfaces.behavior: Generic class with __slots__ value, type, help, _info (line 67). Defaults: type='plain', help=None. Extra **kwargs are kept in _info and read as attributes through __getattr__.
edge_cases: Unknown attribute returns None instead of raising AttributeError
type values the built-in shell scripts handle: plain, dir, file; any other type is ignored by the bash, fish and powershell scripts

interfaces.name: CompletionItem.__getattr__
interfaces.behavior: Returns self._info.get(name), so missing metadata is None (line 100).
edge_cases: Only called for attributes not found normally

interfaces.name: ShellComplete
interfaces.behavior: Base class (line 277, versionadded 8.0). Holds cli, ctx_args, prog_name, complete_var. Subclasses must set the class vars `name` and `source_template`.
edge_cases: get_completion_args and format_completion are abstract and raise NotImplementedError in the base class
The base class can be used directly to call get_completions (tests do this)

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.__init__
interfaces.behavior: Stores cli, ctx_args (a mutable mapping), prog_name and complete_var (line 306).
edge_cases: ctx_args is later mutated by _resolve_context, which sets resilient_parsing=True

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.func_name
interfaces.behavior: Property (line 318). Replaces '-' with '_' in prog_name, strips non-word ASCII characters with re.sub(r'\W*', '', flags=re.ASCII), and returns f'_{safe}_completion'.
edge_cases: A prog_name with only symbols gives '__completion'

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.source_vars
interfaces.behavior: Returns the dict used to format source_template (line 326), with keys complete_func (func_name), complete_var and prog_name.
edge_cases: Subclasses can add keys, though the _SourceVarsDict TypedDict only declares three

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.source
interfaces.behavior: Returns source_template % source_vars() (line 338).
edge_cases: A literal '%' in a custom template must be written as '%%', otherwise the formatting fails
The result is encoded and written without a trailing newline by shell_complete

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Abstract (line 346). Must return (args, incomplete) read from env vars.

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.get_completions
interfaces.behavior: Line 353. Calls _resolve_context, then _resolve_incomplete, then obj.shell_complete(ctx, incomplete). Returns a list of CompletionItem.
edge_cases: Empty incomplete is allowed
args may be mutated by _resolve_incomplete (an '--opt=value' split appends the option name)

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Abstract (line 367). Turns one CompletionItem into the shell wire string.

interfaces.name: ShellComplete.complete
interfaces.behavior: Line 375. Calls get_completion_args, then get_completions, then format_completion on each item. Joins the results with '\n'.
edge_cases: No completions gives an empty string; shell_complete's echo then still adds a newline
The result has no trailing newline of its own, since echo adds one

interfaces.name: BashComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='bash', template _SOURCE_BASH (line 388). The script runs `env COMP_WORDS=... COMP_CWORD=... VAR=bash_complete $1`, then handles types: dir sets compopt -o dirnames, file sets compopt -o default, plain appends to COMPREPLY. The script registers with `complete -o nosort`, which needs Bash >= 4.4.
edge_cases: The bash script ignores item.help

interfaces.name: BashComplete._check_version
interfaces.behavior: Static method (line 394). Finds bash with shutil.which and runs `bash --norc -c 'echo ${BASH_VERSION}'`. Prints a translated warning to stderr if the version is below 4.4, or if bash is not found or the version can't be parsed.
edge_cases: Never aborts; it only warns on stderr
The version comparison is done on strings, so '10' < '4' is True (a bug for major versions >= 10)
Tests monkeypatch it

interfaces.name: BashComplete.source
interfaces.behavior: Calls _check_version(), then super().source() (line 427).
edge_cases: Runs a subprocess on every source call

interfaces.name: BashComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Line 431. Splits env COMP_WORDS with split_arg_string. cword=int(env COMP_CWORD). args=cwords[1:cword]. incomplete=cwords[cword], or '' on IndexError.
edge_cases: A missing env var raises KeyError
A non-integer COMP_CWORD raises ValueError

interfaces.name: BashComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Returns f'{type},{value}' (line 443). The help text is dropped.
edge_cases: A value containing a comma or newline is not escaped; the script does `IFS=',' read type value`, which keeps the rest of the line in value

interfaces.name: ZshComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='zsh', template _SOURCE_ZSH (line 447). The script uses _describe for items with help and compadd for items without. It is frozen for backwards compatibility, so changes go into format_completion.

interfaces.name: ZshComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Line 465. help_ = item.help or '_'. Escapes ':' as '\:' in the value only when help is present (not '_'). Returns 'type\nvalue\nhelp'.
edge_cases: A real help text of '_' is treated as no help
A multi-line help is not sanitized

interfaces.name: ZshComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Same as BashComplete: COMP_WORDS and COMP_CWORD, args=cwords[1:cword] (line 453).
edge_cases: Missing env var raises KeyError
Non-integer COMP_CWORD raises ValueError

interfaces.name: FishComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='fish', template _SOURCE_FISH (line 479). get_completion_args (line 485) reads COMP_WORDS (the whole command line) and COMP_CWORD (the current token, not an index). The incomplete word is split_arg_string(COMP_CWORD)[0] when non-empty. args=cwords[1:], and the last element is popped if it equals incomplete.
edge_cases: COMP_CWORD='' gives an empty incomplete
A quoted partial word is unquoted
A missing env var raises KeyError

interfaces.name: FishComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Line 499. With help: 'type,value\thelp', where newlines in the help become literal backslash-n and tabs become spaces. Without help: 'type,value'.
edge_cases: An empty help string is treated as no help

interfaces.name: PowerShellComplete
interfaces.behavior: name='powershell', template _SOURCE_POWERSHELL (line 516, versionadded 8.5.0). The template uses Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native and parses the output 3 lines at a time. Types: plain gives a CompletionResult with a tooltip; dir and file use Get-ChildItem with a prefix glob.
edge_cases: The prefix for dir/file is wordToComplete+'*'

interfaces.name: PowerShellComplete.format_completion
interfaces.behavior: Line 537. Same 3-line format as zsh. Help has \r and \n replaced by spaces ('_' if no help). The value is not escaped.
edge_cases: CRLF becomes two spaces
A value containing a newline would break the framing

interfaces.name: PowerShellComplete.get_completion_args
interfaces.behavior: Same logic as Bash and Zsh (line 525).
edge_cases: Missing env var raises KeyError

interfaces.name: add_completion_class
interfaces.behavior: Registers cls in the module-level `_available_shells` under name or cls.name and returns cls, so it works as a decorator (line 560).
edge_cases: Overwrites an existing entry silently
No validation of the name
If name is None and the class has no `name` attribute, AttributeError is raised

interfaces.name: get_completion_class
interfaces.behavior: Dict lookup in _available_shells (line 588). It has typing overloads for 'bash', 'fish' and 'zsh' only (no powershell overload).
edge_cases: Unknown name returns None

interfaces.name: split_arg_string
interfaces.behavior: Line 598. A shlex.shlex posix=True, whitespace_split=True, commenters='' split. On ValueError (unclosed quote or trailing escape) it appends lex.token as the partial token. Moved here from parser in 8.2.
edge_cases: Unclosed quote keeps the partial token without the quote
Trailing backslash is dropped
Empty string gives []

claim.error_conventions: The module has no custom exception types. shell_complete signals failure through a return code of 1, with no message. The bash version check prints translated messages to stderr with echo(err=True) and does not raise; the messages are sentences with no 'Error:' prefix. The abstract methods raise bare NotImplementedError. Bad environment variables (missing COMP_WORDS or COMP_CWORD, or a non-integer COMP_CWORD) surface as raw KeyError or ValueError from os.environ and int(). The completion code assumes make_context runs with resilient_parsing=True, so Click usage errors are suppressed during resolution.

examples.description: Base ShellComplete used to get completions directly in tests
Option name completion hides options already used
Registering a custom shell by decorator
Full complete via env var instruction
examples.code:
cli = Group("cli", commands=[Command("a"), Command("b", help="bee")])
env["_CLI_COMPLETE"] = f"{shell}_complete"
result = runner.invoke(cli, env=env)

c = CompletionItem("test", a=1)
assert c.a == 1
assert c.b is None

tests.how_it_asserts: Plain pytest asserts. Most tests call a local helper that builds ShellComplete(cli, {}, name, '_CLICK_COMPLETE') and compare the list of .value strings from get_completions. Cases covered: groups, chained groups, options, arguments, nargs, `--`, hidden params, Choice, Path and File types, and context_settings. The end-to-end tests use the `runner` fixture with env={'_CLI_COMPLETE': '<shell>_source|complete', COMP_WORDS, COMP_CWORD} and compare result.output exactly or by substring. BashComplete._check_version is monkeypatched out. Registry tests use a fixture that saves, clears and restores `_available_shells`. Other tests check the LF-only line endings of source output, zsh colon escaping, fish and PowerShell help escaping via format_completion, and no ResourceWarning from unclosed files. Some of these tests I saw only by name, not in full.

extension_points.name: _available_shells / add_completion_class
extension_points.what_could_attach: Register new ShellComplete subclasses (for example nushell, elvish or tcsh) with a name, a source_template, and get_completion_args and format_completion implementations.

extension_points.name: ShellComplete.source_vars
extension_points.what_could_attach: Override to add template variables, or to tweak the generated script per class.

extension_points.name: ShellComplete.format_completion
extension_points.what_could_attach: Override to change the wire format, for example escaping values or passing the CompletionItem's extra metadata to a custom shell script.

extension_points.name: ShellComplete.get_completions
extension_points.what_could_attach: Override to filter, sort or post-process the CompletionItem list before formatting.

extension_points.name: CompletionItem type/kwargs
extension_points.what_could_attach: New item types (beyond plain, dir, file) or extra kwargs, used by custom type completions and a matching custom shell script.

extension_points.name: _resolve_incomplete
extension_points.what_could_attach: Dispatch point that picks the Command or Parameter whose shell_complete(ctx, incomplete) is called. Custom Parameter, Command or ParamType shell_complete methods plug in here.

extension_points.name: source_template class var
extension_points.what_could_attach: Replace the script text on a subclass, for example to extend the bash script to use help text.

gaps.description: Bash script ignores help text and CompletionItem.help. There is no descriptive completion for bash.
gaps.why_plausible: The bash wire format already carries only type and value, but the other shells carry help. Bash 5.x can show descriptions through a custom display approach.

gaps.description: Value escaping is inconsistent. Bash and PowerShell values containing commas or newlines are not escaped, and zsh help is not newline-sanitized.
gaps.why_plausible: Fish and PowerShell already sanitize help text, so the same treatment applies to zsh help and to values.

gaps.description: get_completion_class has no typing overload for 'powershell'. The Bash version check compares version strings lexicographically and breaks for majors >= 10.
gaps.why_plausible: Small fixes that follow the existing patterns.

gaps.description: No auto-detection of the shell, and no built-in install command that writes the script to the shell's rc or completions directory.
gaps.why_plausible: The `source` instruction already produces the script, so a helper could wrap it for the user.

gaps.description: Env var parsing failures (KeyError or ValueError) are not handled gracefully in get_completion_args.
gaps.why_plausible: Shell scripts could be invoked incorrectly, and a clean exit code would be friendlier.

limitations: The shell is parsed with instruction.partition('_'), so registered shell names cannot contain underscores.
The zsh script is frozen for backwards compatibility, so only format_completion can change zsh behavior.
Bash completion requires Bash >= 4.4 (the nosort option). The check only warns on stderr, and the string comparison of versions is buggy for majors >= 10.
The source output has no trailing newline (nl=False). The complete output is utf-8 encoded bytes.
Completion runs with resilient_parsing=True and does not invoke callbacks or prompts. _resolve_context mutates the passed ctx_args.
Options are recognized through ctx._opt_prefixes, a private attribute.
The PowerShell script treats the dir and file types with a Get-ChildItem glob on the prefix and ignores the item's value.
Only the plain, dir and file item types are understood by the built-in scripts.
